text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALES - The Taiwan Flour Mills Association bought 72,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat. For Dec 15-Jan 5 shipment it bought 16,600 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat (DNS) at $196.67 per tonne, 10,700 of hard red winter (HRW) at $191.70 and white wheat at $155.30. Freight was fixed at $19.5-. For Dec 30-Jan 20 it bought 22,400 DNS at $195.30, 9,400 HRW at $190.87 and 6,200 white at $155.25.

WHEAT TENDERS - South Korea's Korea Feed Association (KFA) said Wednesday it passed on tenders for 105,000 tonnes of feed wheat. A KFA official said it sought wheat near $136 per tonne, C and F, but offers were more than $140.

- Sri Lanka is expected to soon seek 100,000 tonnes of optional origin wheat for delivery in January and February. Potential suppliers could include the United States, Argentina, Australian and Canada, European grain traders said.
WHEAT TENDERS - Tunisia Wednesday was seeking 100,000 tonnes of optional-origin soft wheat to be shipped in January and February, European grain traders said.

- Turkey will invite bids December 10 to import 200,000 tonnes of red and white milling wheat on a three-year credit basis, a grain official said. He said the imports would be from either the United States, Australia, Argentina or any European Union member country.
SOYBEAN TENDER - South Korea is to tender for 55,000 tonnes No.1 optional-origin soybeans late Wednesday for December-January shipment.
LENTIL TENDER - Syria offered 9,500 tonnes of lentils for export. December 16 was set as final date for bids and results will be announced on December 17.

MARKET TALK - India's wheat exports will total 1.5 million tonnes in 1996, a senior government official said during a visit to London. S.P. Jakhanwal, government secretary in charge of food procurement and distribution at the Ministry of Food, said India had completed wheat exports for this year and had no more to sell...

MARKET TALK - India's 1997 rice exports are forecast at 1.8 million tonnes, 50 percent less than in 1996 but still well above historical levels. Diminishing government-owned food grain stocks have prompted the government to reverse policies designed to improve the availability of rice for export, according to a report from the U.S. Agriculture Department attache in India.
